title.narrative: Caribbean Resilient Renewable Energy Infrastructure Investment Facility

description.narrative: The Project Development Objective is to increase the share of utility-scale renewable energy generation in the Caribbean countries.

The proposed Additional Financing (AF) provides US$3.0 million in Korea World Bank Partnership Facility (KWPF) grant resources, US$1.5 million each to Grenada and Saint Lucia, to deepen and accelerate grid modernization under the Caribbean Resilient Renewable Energy Infrastructure Investment Facility (RREIIF, P180831). Under Component 3, the AF will finance the design, supply, installation, commissioning, and operationalization of digital substations at priority grid sites in both countries. This includes digital protection relays, intelligent electronic devices (IEDs), process bus and station bus infrastructure, and monitoring and control systems linked to existing SCADA platforms. Knowledge exchange study tours to the Republic of Korea will allow utility and government personnel to draw on KEPCO's recognized smart grid expertise. For Saint Lucia, the AF also reallocates US$1.0 million to the scholarship and apprenticeship program under Subcomponent 3.4(b), expanding support for men and women pursuing careers in electrical, civil, and mechanical engineering and related energy-sector fields. The AF will be implemented from 2026 to 2029 within the parent project's existing institutional framework and December 31, 2032 closing date.The AF complements the parent operation by addressing a critical grid infrastructure gap that affects the success of other renewable energy investments under RREIIF. Component 3 investments in transmission and distribution infrastructure and battery energy storage systems create the physical capacity to connect utility-scale renewable generation. The digital substations financed under this AF add the real-time monitoring, automated protection, and advanced grid control needed to safely and reliably integrate higher shares of variable renewable energy in Grenada and Saint Lucia's small island power systems. By enabling smarter, more resilient grid management, the AF is expected to support the parent project's PDO indicators, including increased renewable energy capacity enabled, annual renewable energy generation, greenhouse gas emissions reduced, and private capital mobilized. It will also generate two dedicated Intermediate Results: digital substations designed and operationalized, and utility personnel engaged in knowledge exchange. Beyond Grenada and Saint Lucia, the AF's standardized smart grid specifications and lessons can support future application in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines under SOP1, countries joining in SOP2, and later phases of RREIIF.
